user.text: The UserDashboard component needs to fetch user-specific data that changes on each request. Implement this component as an async server component to fetch from `https://api.example.com/user/preferences` and display the data. Follow the async server component patterns in this codebase.

history.assistant:
Build succeeded. The route `/` is marked `ƒ (Dynamic) server-rendered on demand` — confirming the `no-store` fetch correctly forces per-request rendering rather than static prerendering.

## Summary

I implemented `app/UserDashboard.tsx` as an async server component following the codebase's existing pattern (from `app/page.tsx`).

Per the project rules, I read the Next.js v16 docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` first, since this version has breaking changes. The key finding from the [`fetch` API reference](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/fetch.md) and the [Fetching Data guide](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/06-fetching-data.md):

- The default `auto no cache` fetches on every request in dev, but fetches **once at build time** when a route is statically prerendered (no request-time APIs detected). That would bake in stale data — wrong for "data that changes on each request."
- `cache: 'no-store'` guarantees the resource is fetched from the remote server on **every request**, even without request-time APIs.

So I used `cache: 'no-store'` to satisfy the per-request requirement, and kept the codebase's try/catch-with-mock-fallback pattern so the build doesn't fail when `api.example.com` is unreachable.

What I changed:
- `app/UserDashboard.tsx`: converted the stub into `export default async function UserDashboard`, with a separate `getUserPreferences()` async fetcher hitting `https://api.example.com/user/preferences` using `cache: 'no-store'`, a typed `UserPreferences` shape, a mock-data fallback on error, and a rendered list of the preferences.

Verification:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.
- `npx next build` → exit 0; route `/` reported as `ƒ (Dynamic) server-rendered on demand`, confirming per-request fetching.

One thing to flag: the displayed fields (`theme`, `language`, `notifications`) are assumptions about the API's response shape since the endpoint is a placeholder. If the real `api.example.com/user/preferences` returns a different schema, the `UserPreferences` type and the rendered list should be adjusted to match.

11	Welcome to the Next.js documentation!
12	
13	## What is Next.js?
14	
15	Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.
16	
17	It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.
18	
19	Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.
20	
21	## How to use the docs
22	
23	The docs are organized into 3 sections:
24	
25	- [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
26	- [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
27	- [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.
28	
29	Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.
30	
31	## App Router and Pages Router
32	
33	Next.js has two different routers:
34	
35	- **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
36	- **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.
37	
38	At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.
39	
40	### React version handling
41	
42	The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:
43	
44	- **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.
45	
46	- **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.
47	
48	This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.
49	
50	## Pre-requisite knowledge
51	
52	Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:
53	
54	- HTML
55	- CSS
56	- JavaScript
57	- React
58	
59	If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.
60	
61	## Accessibility
62	
63	For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.
64	
65	## Join our Community
66	
67	If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

2  	title: Caching
3  	description: Learn how to cache data and UI in Next.js
4  	related:
5  	  title: Next Steps
6  	  description: Learn more about revalidation and the APIs mentioned on this page.
7  	  links:
8  	    - app/getting-started/revalidating
9  	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
10 	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
11 	    - app/guides/instant-navigation
12 	---
13 	
14 	> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
15 	
16 	Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.
17 	
18 	## Enabling Cache Components
19 	
20 	New App Router apps created with the recommended [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) defaults already have Cache Components enabled.
21 	
22 	To enable it in an existing or manually created app, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:
23 	
24 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
25 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
26 	
27 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
28 	  cacheComponents: true,
29 	}
30 	
31 	export default nextConfig
32 	```
33 	
34 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
35 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
36 	const nextConfig = {
37 	  cacheComponents: true,
38 	}
39 	
40 	module.exports = nextConfig
41 	```
42 	
43 	> **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details.
44 	
45 	## Usage
46 	
47 	The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:
48 	
49 	- **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`)
50 	- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)
51 	
52 	A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).
53 	
54 	> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
55 	
56 	Arguments and any values captured from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. See [cache output](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-output) for what an entry holds, and [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work.
57 	
58 	### Data-level caching
59 	
60 	To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body:
61 	
62 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
63 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
64 	
65 	export async function getUsers() {
66 	  'use cache'
67 	  cacheLife('hours')
68 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
69 	}
70 	```
71

13 	
14 	> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
15 	
16 	Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.
17 	
18 	## Enabling Cache Components
19 	
20 	New App Router apps created with the recommended [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) defaults already have Cache Components enabled.
21 	
22 	To enable it in an existing or manually created app, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:
23 	
24 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
25 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
26 	
27 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
28 	  cacheComponents: true,
29 	}
30 	
31 	export default nextConfig
32 	```
33 	
34 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
35 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
36 	const nextConfig = {
37 	  cacheComponents: true,
38 	}
39 	
40 	module.exports = nextConfig
41 	```
42 	
43 	> **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details.
44 	
45 	## Usage
46 	
47 	The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:
48 	
49 	- **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`)
50 	- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)
51 	
52 	A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).
53 	
54 	> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
55 	
56 	Arguments and any values captured from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. See [cache output](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-output) for what an entry holds, and [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work.
57 	
58 	### Data-level caching
59 	
60 	To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body:
61 	
62 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
63 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
64 	
65 	export async function getUsers() {
66 	  'use cache'
67 	  cacheLife('hours')
68 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
69 	}
70 	```
